components.title: Buttons
components.description: Buttons trigger actions. Text is Titillium 16px semibold with 0.4px letter-spacing on a pill shape; an icon is optional and always goes with a visible label. Hover and keyboard focus share the elevated state.

examples.title: Primary and secondary
examples.note: Primary: --bt-color-primary fill with white text. Secondary: white fill with primary text. Use one primary action per view; the icon is optional and is hidden from screen readers.

examples.title: Hover and focus
examples.note: The fill (primary) or the text (secondary) turns --bt-color-primary-hover and the button rises with --bt-shadow-button (0 20px 25px -5px, primary at 20%). Keyboard focus shows the same state plus the focus ring.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.note: Disabled buttons use their own colors (bluetab-blue-10 fill, bluetab-blue-30 text) instead of opacity, lose the shadow and cannot be focused. WCAG does not require contrast for disabled controls, but explain why an action is unavailable.

examples.title: Other variants
Button sizes
examples.note: lg reproduces the design frame (60px); md is the default for forms, sm and xs for toolbars and tables. Every size keeps the same type, colors and states.
examples.html:
<button class="bt-button bt-button--xs">Extra small</button>
<button class="bt-button bt-button--sm">Small</button>
<button class="bt-button">Medium</button>
<button class="bt-button bt-button--lg">Large</button>

components.title: Motion
components.description: Motion explains what changed: where an element comes from and where it goes. BDS uses six duration tokens and productive or expressive easing curves; entrances decelerate, exits accelerate and are shorter, and everything is disabled with prefers-reduced-motion.

examples.title: Duration tokens
examples.note: Match the duration to the size and distance of the change: fast for small feedback, moderate for menus and dialogs, slow for panels and page content. Press play to compare.
examples.html:
fast-01 70ms
moderate-02 240ms
slow-02 700ms

examples.title: Easing curves
examples.note: Productive curves for everyday UI; expressive curves for moments that should be noticed (a dialog opening, a success). Entrance decelerates into place, exit accelerates away, standard moves between two states.
examples.html:
standard
expressive-entrance

examples.title: Enter and exit
examples.note: Elements that appear fade and scale or slide in with ease-entrance; when they leave they use ease-exit and a shorter duration. Utility classes: bt-motion-fade-in, bt-motion-slide-up, bt-motion-scale-in, bt-motion-slide-in-right.
examples.html:
Fade in
Slide up
Scale in

examples.title: Expand and collapse
examples.note: Accordions animate their height; dialogs, menus and snackbars animate in and out from CSS alone (@starting-style), so they need no JavaScript.
examples.html: The content height animates with the moderate-02 token.

examples.title: Reduced motion
examples.note: When the operating system asks for reduced motion, reset.css cuts every animation and transition to ~0ms: state changes stay instant and nothing moves. Never convey information through motion alone.
examples.html:
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
  }
}
